Drone incursions trigger air alerts across Lithuania, NATO jets scrambled

Drone incursions prompted yellow and red air alerts across large parts of Lithuania overnight, with NATO fighter jets scrambled on both occasions, but the drones were not shot down and flew into Latvian airspace, Lithuanian officials said Wednesday.

The first yellow alert was declared in the Vilnius and Utena regions at around 23:00 Tuesday and lifted shortly after midnight. Almost immediately, a second alert was issued, initially in the Alytus region before being expanded to much of central and northern Lithuania. The warning was subsequently upgraded from yellow to red, meaning that residents in the regions were to take shelter.

Vilmantas Vitkauskas, head of the National Crisis Management Centre, said three drones had initially been detected in Belarus, but none entered Lithuanian airspace.

“At around 21:30, we received a warning about possible balloons and potential disruptions to airspace. The initial airport closure took place in Vilnius, followed by Kaunas. As the situation escalated and the drones entered, the airspace was closed again,” Vitkauskas said.

Preliminary information indicated that only three flights at Vilnius Airport were affected, involving more than 400 passengers, he added.
